subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers Khel Ratna and Dronacharya awards.

questions.stem: What is the highest sporting honor in India, awarded annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports?

options.option_text: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award
Arjuna Award
Dronacharya Award
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honor. It is awarded for "spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of four years" at international level. The award was originally called the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna but was renamed in 2021 to honor hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand. 
DECOY BUSTING: The Arjuna Award is the second-highest honor, given for consistently good performance over 4 years. The Dronacharya Award is exclusively for sports COACHES. The MAKA Trophy is awarded to the top overall performing University in inter-university tournaments.
EXAM INSIGHT: Viswanathan Anand (Chess) was the very first recipient of this award in 1991-92. The award carries a cash prize of Rs 25 lakhs, a medal, and a certificate of honor.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which national sports award is given exclusively to coaches who have produced medal winners at prestigious international events?

options.option_text: Dronacharya Award
Arjuna Award
Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement
Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Dronacharya Award, named after the legendary guru of the Pandavas and Kauravas in the Mahabharata, is specifically dedicated to outstanding coaches in sports and games. Instituted in 1985, it honors coaches who have consistently trained athletes to achieve excellence at international events like the Olympics, Asian Games, and World Championships.
DECOY BUSTING: The Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement (not to be confused with the Khel Ratna) is given to retired sportspersons for their lifetime contribution. The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar is given to corporate entities and NGOs that promote sports.
EXAM INSIGHT: O.M. Nambiar (coach of P.T. Usha), Om Prakash Bhardwaj (Boxing), and Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat (Wrestling) were the first recipients of the Dronacharya Award in 1985.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy is presented annually to the best-performing institution in which category?

options.option_text: State Sports Authorities for regional league standings
Universities for overall inter-university sports performance
School boards for maximum sports enrollment nationally
National Sports Federations for international medal tally

questions.explanation: The MAKA Trophy is awarded to the top-performing university at the All India Inter-University Sports and Games competitions organised by the Association of Indian Universities. It is not given to state sports bodies or schools — a common confusion since candidates often conflate it with state-level trophies or federation rankings.

questions.stem: In which year was the Arjuna Award, recognising outstanding sporting achievement over the preceding four years, first instituted by the Government of India?

options.option_text: 1961 — the year India's national sports award framework was established
1947 — marking independence and the launch of national honours
1956 — coinciding with the Melbourne Summer Olympics campaign
1972 — aligned with major post-Munich Olympic policy reforms

questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961 by the Ministry of Education (now Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports). Option C (1956) is the most tempting distractor as it coincides with the Melbourne Olympics, but the award came five years later; 1947 and 1972 have no link to the award's founding.

questions.stem: The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award recognises achievement in adventure sports. Across how many domain categories is this award presented each year?

options.option_text: Two categories covering only land and marine sea adventures
Four categories including underwater and space frontier sports
Three categories covering land, water, and air adventures
Five categories spanning all extreme sports disciplines listed

questions.explanation: The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award is presented in exactly three categories: Adventure on Land, Adventure on Water/Sea, and Adventure in Air. Option A is the most common mistake — candidates recall 'land and water' but forget the air category, which covers paragliding, skydiving, and similar disciplines.

questions.stem: Which eligibility criterion uniquely distinguishes the Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement from the Arjuna Award for Outstanding Performance?

options.option_text: Requires a minimum of one Olympic or Asian Games medal in career
Awarded exclusively to athletes who represent India at the Olympics
Open only to team sport athletes, excluding individual sport performers
Honours post-retirement contribution to sports development and promotion

questions.explanation: The Dhyan Chand Award specifically recognises contribution to sports development and promotion made after retirement from active competition — through coaching, administration, or advocacy. The Arjuna Award, by contrast, rewards peak-career on-field performance. No Olympic medal is mandated for either award, making Option A a plausible but incorrect distractor.

questions.stem: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar differs structurally from other national sports awards because it is primarily conferred on which class of awardees?

options.option_text: State Olympic associations that organise national championships
Corporate entities, sports bodies, and institutions promoting sports
Media organisations covering Indian athletes at international events
Defence and paramilitary forces producing national-level athletes

questions.explanation: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar is uniquely awarded to organisations — corporates, NGOs, sports bodies — that have made significant contributions to promoting sports in India, not to individual athletes or coaches. This structural distinction makes it the odd one out in the national sports awards framework.

questions.stem: Prime Minister Modi announced the renaming of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award on National Sports Day. What is the direct significance of that date in relation to the award's new name?

options.option_text: August 15 is Major Dhyan Chand's recorded date of retirement from hockey
August 29 is Major Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary and National Sports Day
August 29 is the anniversary of India's first Olympic gold medal in hockey
August 15 marks the founding of the Indian Hockey Federation in 1947

questions.explanation: National Sports Day falls on August 29, the birthday of Major Dhyan Chand (born 1905), the hockey wizard after whom the award was renamed in 2021. Option C is the sharpest distractor — India did win hockey gold at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, but that event has no fixed August 29 link; the date is Dhyan Chand's birthday, which is why it was chosen for the announcement.

questions.stem: Since 2017, the Dronacharya Award for Sports Coaching is presented in two distinct sub-categories. Which combination correctly names both?

options.option_text: Regular Category for active coaches and Lifetime Category for coaches after retirement
Senior Category for Olympic coaches and Junior Category for school-level coaches
National Category for domestic coaches and International Category for overseas postings
Professional Category for full-time coaches and Amateur Category for part-time coaches

questions.explanation: From 2017 onwards, the Dronacharya Award has two categories: Regular (for coaches with consistent recent high-performance output) and Lifetime (for coaches with decades of sustained contribution to Indian sport). None of the other splits — Senior/Junior, National/International, or Professional/Amateur — exist in the award's official structure, though Senior/Junior sounds plausible enough to mislead.

questions.stem: National Sports Day in India is observed on 29 August every year. This date commemorates the birth anniversary of which hockey legend after whom the Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is named?

options.option_text: Balbir Singh Sr., three-time Olympic gold medallist
Dhyan Chand, the 'Wizard of Hockey' and Olympian
K. D. Singh Babu, the Padma Shri-winning forward
Leslie Claudius, four-time Olympic medal winner

questions.explanation: Major Dhyan Chand, born 29 August 1905, is celebrated as the greatest hockey player ever; National Sports Day marks his birth anniversary and the Khel Ratna was renamed after him in 2021. Balbir Singh Sr. and Leslie Claudius are also celebrated Olympians but neither gives their name to the award or to National Sports Day.

questions.stem: Which sports award carries a cash prize of ₹5 lakh and a plaque, and is specifically given to recognise outstanding performance by a sportsperson in the year immediately preceding the award — making it more 'recent-form' focused than the Arjuna Award?

options.option_text: Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award for lifetime contribution
Arjuna Award for four years of sustained achievement
Dronacharya Award for coaches of award-winning athletes
Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna — highest honour for one-year peak

questions.explanation: The Khel Ratna (now Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna) is India's highest sporting honour and evaluates performance primarily in the year preceding the award cycle, whereas the Arjuna Award explicitly requires four years of consistent achievement. The Dronacharya recognises coaching, not personal performance.

questions.stem: The Arjuna Award statuette depicts Arjuna in the act of aiming his bow. A sportsperson must have NOT been convicted of doping or indulged in match-fixing during the last how many years to remain eligible for the award?

options.option_text: Last 2 years preceding the nomination deadline
Last 3 years preceding the nomination deadline
Last 4 years preceding the nomination deadline
Last 5 years preceding the nomination deadline

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports guidelines specify that a nominee must be free from doping or match-fixing offences for the last four years — the same window used to assess sustained performance. Candidates often confuse this with the 2-year ban period under WADA or the 5-year rule sometimes associated with lifetime awards.

questions.stem: The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy is awarded to the best overall sports-performing university. Which of the following correctly describes the prize structure of the MAKA Trophy?

options.option_text: A rolling trophy only, with no cash component attached
A trophy plus ₹10 lakh for the winner university's sports fund
A trophy, cash prize, and a certificate for the runner-up
Separate trophies for men's and women's divisions of universities

questions.explanation: The MAKA Trophy awards a trophy and cash prize to the overall winner and also provides a runner-up certificate/award, recognising second-best performance. It is not gender-divided into separate trophies and is not a rolling trophy without monetary component. Many candidates confuse it with purely symbolic awards.

questions.stem: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar is conferred on organisations, not individuals. Which of the following categories is NOT an official category under this award?

options.option_text: Identification and nurturing of budding/young talent
Encouragement to sports through Corporate Social Responsibility
Employment of sports persons in government services
Sports for development among persons with disabilities

questions.explanation: The four official categories of the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar are: (1) identification and nurturing of young talent, (2) encouragement through CSR, (3) sports for development among persons with disabilities, and (4) promotion of sports through Panchayati Raj/urban local bodies. 'Employment of sports persons in government services' is not a designated category; it is a common distractor because sports quotas in government jobs are a known policy but not a category of this award.

questions.stem: Among the disciplines listed below, which one falls under the 'Land Adventure' sub-category of the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award, rather than the 'Water' or 'Air' sub-categories?

options.option_text: Open-water marathon swimming across international straits
High-altitude mountaineering and rock-face expedition
Solo trans-oceanic sailing voyage in a yacht
Skydiving and free-fall parachuting from stratosphere

questions.explanation: The Tenzing Norgay Award has three sub-categories — Land, Water, and Air. Mountaineering and rock climbing are squarely in the Land category, which Tenzing Norgay himself exemplified. Open-water swimming and sailing fall under Water, while skydiving/parachuting falls under Air. Candidates often misplace mountaineering under 'Air' because of high altitude, which is incorrect.

questions.stem: The Selection Committee for national sports awards includes representatives from various bodies. Which combination correctly identifies two permanent/ex-officio members on the Arjuna Award Selection Committee?

options.option_text: Secretary, Sports Authority of India + Chairman, Indian Olympic Association
Secretary, Dept. of Sports + Director General, Sports Authority of India
Union Sports Minister + President, Indian Olympic Association
Chief of Army Staff + Secretary General, Olympic Gold Quest

questions.explanation: The Selection Committee for national sports awards is chaired by a retired judge or eminent person and includes the Secretary of the Department of Sports and the Director General of SAI as ex-officio members, along with Arjuna awardees, sports journalists, and federation nominees. The Sports Minister does not sit on the committee (executive separation), and IOA's president is not an ex-officio member. This is a frequently muddled question because IOA's visibility in Indian sport misleads candidates.
